messages:
Anna: Quick sync — we're locking the embeddings ingest defaults for the vNext API. Two quick design points I want alignment on: (1) clipping behavior (token vs char/byte) and (2) response payload format (numeric arrays vs packed base64 float32). Also want a recommended pattern to preserve client ordering when some items fail.

Mike: I lean token-based clipping. Runtime already reasons in tokens for performance; char/byte clipping is unpredictable for model inputs. Suggest a `clip_strategy` param: `token_truncate` (default) or `char_truncate`.

Joseph: +1 token_truncate. About format — packed base64 float32 is attractive for bandwidth, but breaks a lot of client SDKs. Proposal: default `format: "arrays"` (current behavior), support opt-in `format: "packed_b64"`. Add an explicit `content_encoding` field so clients can negotiate.

Tasha: runtime note: decoding/encoding packed float32 costs CPU and extra memcpy. Packed_b64 reduces wire but increases host-side CPU — need perf numbers. Also packed format complicates streaming/partial results.

Lee: product perspective: enterprise customers need stable vector dims and guaranteed ordering. Can we pass through a client-provided id per item (e.g., `client_id`) so they can reconcile asynchronously? Also define exact behavior for empty string vs null input.

Mike: Draft response envelope idea — keep HTTP 200 with per-item statuses (avoid multipart codes). Example response (default arrays):

```json
{
  "model": "embed-foo-v1",
  "items": [
    {"client_id": "a1", "status": "ok", "vector": [0.001, -0.32, ...]},
    {"client_id": "a2", "status": "failed", "error": "input too long", "vector": null}
  ],
  "meta": {"requested_format": "arrays", "applied_clip": "token_truncate"}
}
```

For packed_b64 we'd set `vector` to a base64 string and `meta.requested_format: "packed_b64"`. Keep top-level ordering equal to input order.

Joseph: Clarify ordering guarantees: runtime will preserve input order in `items`. If clients submit unordered maps, they MUST provide `client_id` to re-associate. For partial failures we'll include `status: \"failed\"` and `error` text, vector null. That avoids out-of-band index mapping.

Anna: Good. On clipping semantics: do we clip by model token budget or by a separate `max_input_tokens` param? If server-side tokenization is default, we should document exactly which tokenizer and version we use.

Tasha: We should expose `detected_token_count` per item in debug mode to aid repro. Limits proposal from runtime: default `max_items` = 512, default `max_total_tokens` = 200000 per request, and `max_item_tokens` = per-model seq limit (model-dependent). If a single item exceeds `max_item_tokens` we return 400 with clear body: `{error: 'item_too_long', details: {client_id, tokens}}`.

Mike: For back-compat: add query flag `compat=legacy` (or header `X-Redwood-Compat: legacy`) to force arrays-only response and previous error shapes. Non-compat path may introduce `client_id` echo and `meta` field.

Joseph: Also suggest `vectors_base64: boolean` deprecated — prefer single `format` enum. Add `X-Redwood-Embed-Limits` response header showing applied limits and `X-Redwood-Batch-Id` for traceability.

Tasha: About empty/null inputs: runtime will treat `""` (empty string) as valid and return a vector. `null` will be treated as a no-op and will return `status: \"skipped\"` with vector null (this helps downstream batching when clients intentionally pass placeholders). Document this explicitly.

Mike: Edge-case: when clients send mixed types (string + binary attachments) we should reject with 400 unless they use `multipart/form-data` with explicit `content_type` per item. Not planning to support embedded raw binaries in JSON.

ops-bot: Reminder — API changes need spec PR + changelog entry. Next deploy window: Thu 03:00 UTC. :clock3:

Anna: I'll open the spec PR with these defaults and a backwards-compat section. Will include tests for arrays and packed_b64, and at least one example showing `client_id` reconciliation. @Joseph @Mike can you pick up review?

Joseph: I will draft initial PR today. Also add a small Python example showing how to decode packed_b64 into float32 using numpy.

Lee: Please add a short blurb in breaking-changes doc explaining default remains arrays and packed_b64 is opt-in. Also note token-truncate default and link tokenizer version.

Mike: I'll add runtime guard rails (limit headers, per-item validation) and a test harness. We should decide final limit numbers in the PR.

Anna: Awesome — thanks everyone. Filing PR now and tagging the owners.

Tasha: FYI: I'll run a microbenchmark on packed_b64 vs arrays for embed-foo-v1 and post numbers in the PR comments.

Mike: ping for code review once PR is up.

Anna: Thanks — closing the sync. :white_check_mark:
